The delayed obliteration of the arterial lumen may occur by one of several mechanisms, and it's essential to consider the various factors that contribute to this process. Moreover, on occasion, the flow of blood may elevate the torn distal end of the intima, creating a subintimal dissection that can further compromise the integrity of the artery. Additionally, even though the inner and outer coats of the artery remain intact, an intramural hematoma may form that obliterates the lumen of the artery, leading to a complete blockage of blood flow.
